acceptance_arm.why_value_gate_off: its default flipped ON in #10996; an arm that declares itself OFF must pin the explicit 0 or it measures the predicate's population
acceptance_arm.read_back: The set is CLOSED over the modules named in tests/test_7949_c2_door.py::path_modules — a pointer, not a count, because a count in this field went stale three rounds running — and what `tests/test_7949_c2_door.py` enforces mechanically is the CENSUS over that list, not the list's membership: `path_modules` is a hand-maintained tuple, and every ``TORTOISE_*`` read inside those modules must be classified (arm seam, pin, declared input, or an acknowledged non-seam with a stated reason) or the suite reds. Membership is hand-kept, so a read added to a module OUTSIDE that tuple is not caught by it; the same chain's infrastructure reads (record DSN, packs dir, embedding gates, store connection) are inputs, deliberately outside the partition, and a new derived module is a one-line change to the test's path_modules. Every value is re-read from os.environ after setting and a mismatch REFUSES the run.. Cycle 7 added the two reads the closure was still missing, both consulted on the acceptance path and previously in no pin, no ledger row and no closure: TORTOISE_CONTEXT_ENRICH (context_enrich.enrich_enabled, reached as sdk.capture_session(enrich_fn=_capture_enriched_texts) — it rewrites the text each turn embeds) pinned off (fail-safe OFF, so the pin matches today's behaviour), and TORTOISE_JSON_MODE (model_adapters, default-ON and read per call, flips the request's response_format) pinned to "1". A new read inserted in enrich_enabled() left the closure pin GREEN at the previous head (measured). Cycle 8 added TORTOISE_CHANGE_FEED (change_feed.py, reached via sdk._change_feed_enabled on PointRevised) pinned off: an ambient =1 adds a :GraphEvent to the graph the run writes and the probe's S6 step witness prints that count (measured on one capture of the registered corpus: 2 vs 3 :GraphEvent). Cycle 9 added TORTOISE_IDENTIFIER_TOKENS (sparse.py:226, default-ON, read through projection/entities.py:1208 point_identifier_aliases on the write path), pinned to its shipped default 1: it rewrites search_keys on every :Point the run writes, and the registered corpus yields no aliases either way (measured: 0 of 27 points, 0 of 7 fixtures), so the pin makes the population shell-insensitive without moving a number. tortoise/sparse.py is now in path_modules.. Cycle 10 added TORTOISE_SUBJECT_TAU_HI/_LO (subject_binding.py:189 via bind_point_subjects, read through a PARAMETER so no resolver sees them) pinned unset, and made the closure read LITERALS as well as resolved reads: measured 0.90 -> bound at the defaults, suspected with TORTOISE_SUBJECT_TAU_HI=0.99, i.e. the :aboutSubject/:aboutObject edge is not written.
